text:
sara_m: quick heads-up — we're onboarding galeon-9b-v1 for evaluation tomorrow. License attached looks weird, flagged as `R-NonComm-1.0` in the repo. can we host evals on the dev cluster?
aj: can you drop the link?
sara_m: https://vendor.example.com/galeon-9b/license.txt
sara_m: snippet: ```
# License: R-NonComm-1.0
You may use this model for non-commercial research and evaluation only. Redistribution of model weights or derivative checkpoints is prohibited without a commercial license. Attribution required when results are published.
```
license-bot: automated-check: license type detected: R-NonComm-1.0. Flags: [non-commercial, no-redistribution, attribution-required]. Recommended: consult legal for hosting/serving.
leo: if we quantize weights for speed (8-bit) and store those artifacts internally, is that "redistribution" or a derivative?
tim_legal: short answer: quantized weights are a derivative. The license's "no redistribution" clause will likely restrict sharing those artifacts outside the org or shipping them in product. Hosting for customers (hosted API or Dedicated for revenue-generating customers) counts as commercial use unless vendor says otherwise.
aj: do we know if "hosting as a service" is considered redistribution here? some licenses treat SaaS differently.
tim_legal: right — this license explicitly forbids commercial use. Even SaaS/hosting that results in commercial benefit for us or a paying customer would be commercial. There's also a separate dimension: if we provide a private deployment (customer runs in their VPC and we only provide orchestration), that may be allowed if the customer has their own commercial license from the vendor. But we cannot assume that.
sara_m: ok. so for internal evals on our dev cluster with no external customers and no paid offering, that's fine?
tim_legal: internal evaluation/research is within the allowed non-commercial scope. Keep it gated: no public demos, no external customers, and do not push quantized or modified weights outside the org.
leo: what about attribution requirements — can we attach a README or notice when we publish eval results internally?
tim_legal: attribution is fine and required for publications, but attribution doesn't waive commercial restrictions. If anyone plans to publish evaluation benchmarks externally, we need to ensure attribution text is included per the license and run the publication by legal first.
aj: vendor negotiation route: do we have contacts to ask for a commercial license or a redistribution carve-out?
sara_m: I've got an email thread with their partnership rep — can escalate to ask for a limited commercial sublicense for Dedicated/hosted use.
tim_legal: recommended steps: 1) Pause any prod rollout. 2) Limit all experiments to internal dev infra. 3) Don't export or share quantized checkpoints externally. 4) Reach out to vendor for a commercial license or an evaluation addendum that permits quantized derivatives and hosting. 5) If vendor refuses, consider alternative models with permissive T&Cs.
opsbot: note created: ML-LEGAL-2026-58 — embargoed until vendor response.
sara_m: thanks @tim_legal — will pause and start outreach. I'll also add the required attribution template to the internal eval doc.
leo: re: benchmarks, i'll run an internal A/B against crimson-8b on the dev cluster and post results in this thread.
aj: :thumbsup:
tim_legal: ping me if vendor asks for logs or eval outputs — we'll scrub anything that might count as redistributed model artifacts before sharing.
sara_m: final: pausing public hosting plans, internal evals only, vendor outreach started. will update thread when i hear back.
